name: Chemical-Ner
description: Dataset for chemical named entity recognition (NER) in biomedical scientific text. Given a sentence from chemical/biomedical literature, the model must extract all chemical entities and assign one of the predefined types (ABBREVIATION, FAMILY, FORMULA, IDENTIFIER, MULTIPLE, NO CLASS, SYSTEMATIC, TRIVIAL).
card_text: This is a text-only dataset of 200 samples for chemical named entity recognition (NER). Each sample contains a scientific sentence or short abstract excerpt (raw_text) and an instruction prompt that asks the model to extract all chemical entities and their types from the raw_text. The possible entity types are ABBREVIATION, FAMILY, FORMULA, IDENTIFIER, MULTIPLE, NO CLASS, SYSTEMATIC, and TRIVIAL. Outputs are formatted as comma-separated 'entity => type' pairs, e.g. 'glucose => TRIVIAL'. The data is drawn from biomedical and chemistry-related literature, so entities include small molecules, drugs, natural products, and chemical classes. The task evaluates exact extraction of entity mentions and their correct type assignment.

context.semantics: Scientific sentence or abstract excerpt from chemical/biomedical literature. It serves as the source text from which chemical entities must be extracted.

question.semantics: Instruction that asks the model to extract all chemical entities and their types from the given raw_text. It lists the possible entity types and specifies the output format 'entity => type' separated by commas.

answer.semantics: Target extraction result containing comma-separated chemical entities paired with their entity types in the format 'entity => type'. It directly answers the prompt by listing all chemical mentions found in the context.

meta.meta_structure_description: Each sample consists of an input object and an output object. The input object contains a raw_text field with a scientific sentence or short excerpt, and a prompt field with an instruction to extract chemical entities and their types. The output object contains a text field with the extracted entities formatted as comma-separated 'entity => type' pairs. No dialog, options, images, tables, or other auxiliary components are present.
